description:
Why: a slice of a large binary keeps the large buffer alive. With fz-nml.1 (#614), every whole-byte slice is a view, and send shares views across processes (deep_copy retains and freezes the SharedBin, as BEAM does). OTP's answer is to let the program choose: binary:referenced_byte_size/1 reports the size of the buffer a binary references, and binary:copy/1 detaches a slice from it (see ../otp/lib/stdlib/src/binary.erl, copy/1 and referenced_byte_size/1, and the notes there on when copying helps). fz has no :binary module. Elixir's String.duplicate/2 is :binary.copy(subject, n) (../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/string.ex:1858).

What:
- lib/binary.fz: defmodule :binary, registered in src/modules/runtime_library.rs next to erlang.fz. It is a thin, guarded fz surface over runtime intrinsics, following lib/erlang.fz and Kernel.byte_size/1:
  - copy(subject) is copy(subject, 1).
  - copy(subject, n), for a binary and an integer n >= 0, is extern "fz" defp fz_binary_copy(binary, integer) :: binary. It always makes a new binary, even for n = 1, as OTP does.
  - referenced_byte_size(binary) is an extern that returns the referenced buffer's byte count. For a ProcBin that is its SharedBin's bytes_len; for an inline heap bitstring it is its own size.
  - Any other argument raises ArgumentError with Elixir's badarg wording (oracle-checked).
- Runtime: fz_binary_copy writes the n repetitions straight into one freshly allocated buffer, with no staging Vec. Heap::alloc_bitstring becomes the special case of a fill-based allocator (allocate len bytes, then let the caller fill them), so the inline/shared choice stays in one place.
- String.duplicate/2 becomes :binary.copy(s, n), and its doubling helpers (doubled/3) are deleted.
- Docs: .agent/docs/any-value.md (views and referenced size) and externs.md, if it lists the intrinsics.

Acceptance:
- Oracle fixture 01338 (fz-nml block) prints exactly what Elixir does: the OTP doc example (A = :binary.copy(<<1>>, 1000); <<b::binary-10, c::binary>> = A; {byte_size, referenced_byte_size} of a, b, c), copy of a large slice whose referenced size equals its byte size, copy/2 with n = 0, 1 and 3, String.duplicate cases, and badarg for non-binaries and negative n.
- Allocation fixture 01339: :binary.copy(s, n) on a large s allocates one buffer of n * byte_size(s) shared bytes (Process.heap_alloc_stats shared_bin_bytes delta), and String.duplicate allocates the same.
- Passes on all three paths; workspace gate at opt-level 1; pins move only by measured falls.

Base: develop (does not wait on #613). On develop, middle slices are still copies, so referenced_byte_size equals byte_size more often. The fixtures must hold both before and after fz-nml.1.
title: :binary.copy/1,2 and :binary.referenced_byte_size/1 work as in OTP on interp, run and build
